note: Item codes e1_item1..e1_item15 ARE the source Stata file's own column names -- the IRW build (data/gilbertmeta.R, dataset 55) melts them unchanged, so there is no positional or renaming step. IVR_Data.dta labels those columns 'Endline assessment question 1'..'15', which ties each code to a question NUMBER but carries no wording; the wording comes from the paper's appendix Table A4 ('Endline assessment test questions'), identical in the IZA DP 15920 and J-PAL WP4445 versions. That number-to-wording tie was then verified against the data rather than assumed: the live per-item proportion correct reproduces appendix Table B3's total-sample column to 2 dp for all 15 items (0.92/0.76/0.67/0.57/0.63/0.35/0.61/0.67/0.68/0.41/0.82/0.84/0.72/0.45/0.65), and the per-item marks recovered from the .dta's raw e1_cog_* variables (5,5,5,5,6,6,4,4,4,6,6,6,6,6,6) match Table B3's 'Marks assigned' column exactly -- see verify_gilbert_meta_55.R. DEVIATION FROM LITERAL TRANSCRIPTION, disclosed: the test was administered one-on-one in Bangla and the administered Bangla wording is NOT in the deposit (the Harvard Dataverse package holds only .dta data and .do files -- no instrument, no questionnaire) nor in either working-paper appendix, so the base fields carry the authors' own English rendering from Table A4 and language=Bengali with no _translated columns (text_source=translated_substitute, the fallback of the 2026-09-01 rule). Table A4's own parenthetical placeholders are kept verbatim, including elided stimuli ('Make a word with the Bengali letter -----.') and glosses of Bangla words ('What is the antonym of the Bangla word (FREEDOM)?'); its typos are kept too ('Read the following word (FARMER)?', 'Does it even or odd?'). SECOND DEVIATION: each of the 15 questions has three grade-level variants (Level 1/Grade 1, Level 2/Grade 2, Level 3/Grades 3 & 4) and a child answered only the one for their level; the IRW table has no grade column, so item_text concatenates all three labelled variants rather than picking one. option_text is blank throughout: these are orally administered open-response tasks scored right/wrong by the assessor, so resp 0/1 has no option wording, and correct_response is blank because no answer key is published and the correct answer differs by level. instructions/section_prompt blank -- the paper prints no participant-facing instructions, only the note 'The test was conducted on a one-on-one basis.' Rights: deposit is CC0 1.0 and the instrument is a study-built assessment, not a commercially published scale; neither 2026-09-04 rights trigger fires.
public_note: The endline assessment was administered orally in Bangla, but the deposit and both working-paper appendices publish only the authors' English rendering of the questions, so the item text shown here is English rather than what children actually heard.
